text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE [P2] Elevated 5xx + latency for /v2/chat generate (prod-west). Alert rule: inference.error_rate > 4% for 10m. See runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/oncall/inference-errors

morgan: i'm taking primary for this alert. i'm on until 18:00 UTC. assigning lee as secondary (runtime). owen for infra on-call, ria for support, harper for security watch.

lee: quick triage — pulling per-cluster 5xx and node-level CPU/memory. running: `curl -s "http://metrics/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total{route=\"/v2/chat\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])"`

own: infra note: nothing obvious on LB for prod-west. but we have a few nodes with high tx errors on eth1. opening cloud case.

ria: support: customers reporting timeouts in the last 8m; i posted a short note to #support-updates and added tenants A and B as impacted. please let me know if SLA escalation needed.

harper: security: preliminary check on auth errors — none so far. i will watch for token/kms anomalies.

morgan: handoff/coverage question — next shift change at 18:00 UTC. i'm handing to @lee primary, @owen secondary. there's a coverage hole 02:00–04:00 UTC tomorrow where we currently have no security buddy. harper can you cover or recommend backup?

harper: i can cover 02:00–04:00 UTC if we need. would prefer a quick async runbook pointer for what to look for.

morgan: runbook snippet i'll paste in thread (short):
- if >3% 5xx sustained: page runtime first (model runtime / container errors).
- if packet drops / node-level errors: page infra.
- if auth failures, secret errors, or suspicious access: page security.
- support handles customer comms and incident status.

morgan: commands i used: 
```bash
# per-cluster 5xx ratio
curl -s "http://metrics/api/v1/query?query=(sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~\"5..\",route=\"/v2/chat\"}[5m])) by (cluster)) / (sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=\"/v2/chat\"}[5m])) by (cluster))" | jq .
# tail runtime logs on affected pod
kubectl logs -n inference -l app=chat-runtime -c runtime --tail=200 --since=15m
# check node tx/rx errors
ssh node-089 'ip -s link show eth1'
```

lee: runtime findings: a subset of pods show repeated `oom-kill` and `kvcache evict` entries right before 5xx burst. increased model memory footprint could be due to new rollout. checking model-version tags on pods.

own: infra follow-up: cloud case opened for NIC flapping; we rolled a replacement node and traffic shifted. early signs show degraded hosts were mostly on that node pool.

morgan: cross-team routing clarification for the runbook (please confirm or correct):
- runtime owns model process errors, OOMs, kv-cache, model version rollbacks.
- infra owns LB, node/network, disk, autoscaler issues.
- security owns auth, secrets, data exfil alerts.
- support owns customer-facing comms and SLA coordination.

harper: that mapping looks good. add: security should be looped if any trace contains secret path or KMS error.

ria: support asks: if mitigation requires a model rollback, who should we notify first? runtime or support?

lee: notify runtime lead + support simultaneously. runtime does the rollback; support posts a customer-facing update after rollback success. set expectation: we will provide an ETA within 15m.

morgan: mitigation steps executed: scaled up runtime replicas in pool-prod-west by +4, rolled back the recent model rollout tag v1.9.2 -> v1.9.1 on affected nodes, and cordoned node-089. error rate dropped from ~7% to ~1.2% in 6 minutes.

own: infra confirm: cloud replaced node-089 and cleared NIC errors. network errors metric back to baseline.

harper: security follow-up: scanned audit logs for 10m window around spike; no suspicious auth patterns. marking security: cleared.

morgan: status: mitigated for paging. leaving monitoring for 40m. preparing short post-incident notes and runbook updates: 
- clarify routing table for pages (runtime v infra v security v support)
- add explicit handoff checklist with coverage gap checks
- add quick commands for triage (metrics, logs, node checks)

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated by morgan and team. Automated follow-up: please file postmortem within 72h if impacting >1 customer or if rollback performed. See templates: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/postmortem-template

morgan: handoff to @lee in 2m. @lee @owen @harper @ria please acknowledge when you accept next shift.

lee: acknowledged — taking primary now. will monitor and update channel if anything regresses.

ria: acknowledged, will keep support updated and prep a customer note if we need rollback communications.

harper: acknowledged, covering 02:00–04:00 UTC. will do a quick audit check at handoff.

own: acknowledged.

morgan: leaving final note: make sure oncall rota reflects 02:00–04:00 security coverage to avoid future gaps. adding runbook PR with routing clarification. :memo:
